articles.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for 1st time ever due to nor'easter
articles.summary: The annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather — for the first time in history. Officials said Wednesday afternoon that the parade is being postponed until Saturday. "The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's said in a statement on Wednesday. A developing storm is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding to the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day. Gov. Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency in neighboring New Jersey on Wednesday. Concerns about whether balloons would be allowed to fly safely mounted as the National Weather Service issued a high-wind warning of potentially "strong and damaging wind gusts," expected to start at 10 a.m. on Thursday and continue through early Friday morning. The agency also warned of moderate-to-heavy rainfall. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledged the "inconvenience" of the rescheduling, but said the move was necessary to protect the safety of participants and spectators. "I know that many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," he said. "I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first." "On Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe," he added. Macy's executive producer Will Coss was unable to confirm whether all acts that were scheduled to perform on Thanksgiving will still be able to participate Saturday, but said he was "optimistic" that organizers will be able to "maintain the parade that we set out to produce." The decision marks the first time the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, although it has previously been modified due to weather disruptions. In 1971, all balloons were grounded ahead of the parade because of gusty winds and heavy rainfall. The city also established regulations in 1998 requiring large balloons to be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph after an incident during the 1997 parade, in which a Cat in the Hat balloon critically injured a woman after it struck a lamppost. articles.title: Vance says Jensen Huang won't need pardon as Nvidia saga looms over Washington
articles.summary: WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE, Ohio (AP) — Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday played down the possibility that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could need a presidential pardon just days before the executive of the AI giant is expected to appear before a congressional committee. Vance told reporters that Justice Department officials and "multiple officials in our national security apparatus" have confirmed that Huang is "under no investigation." The vice president made the remarks after having a Thanksgiving Eve meal with troops at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. The Nvidia CEO resigned earlier this month after acknowledging extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy . He was reinstated 11 days later at the urging of President Donald Trump . "I don't think he needs a pardon at all," Vance said. "I haven't seen any evidence again that he committed a crime. And if there is evidence that he committed a crime, then that's up to relevant authorities to actually bring a prosecution against him." The comments from Vance came after Trump told the New York Post on Tuesday that pardoning Huang is "always an option," but that he did not think it would be necessary. Trump also told the Post he doesn't want Huang to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights under the U.S. Constitution to avoid self-incrimination amid potential criminal prosecution when he appears before lawmakers. Pleading the Fifth allows a person to refuse to answer questions or provide testimonial evidence if doing so could reasonably expose them to criminal prosecution. Huang is scheduled to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview with a trio of panels on Dec. 1, including the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs committees, and the Select Committee on China. Then on Dec. 3, Huang is expected to appear at a public hearing of the Senate Banking Committee. The Nvidia case raises questions about the line between business and politics The board's stunning reversal has spurred questions about its independence and what Trump's role means for the meeting of business and politics. Nvidia and the White House are also facing scrutiny about Trump's relationship with Huang, a close adviser to the president on artificial intelligence issues. The president has repeatedly welcomed Huang to the White House and earlier this year invited him aboard Air Force One for a state visit to China. The New York Times has reported that Trump had previously been briefed on intelligence concerns about the Nvidia CEO's relationship with Alice Huang , an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed. U.S. officials suspected that she was working with China's Ministry of State Security. Beijing has denied it. Congressional staffers from the House and Senate Intelligence Committees and representing chamber leaders received a classified briefing on Tuesday about the matter from intelligence officials, according to two people familiar with the matter who were not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity. Officials from the CIA, FBI, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence were among those on hand for the briefing, one of the people said. "We don't try people in the court of public opinion. We don't try people based on anonymously sourced stories in the New York Times, we try people based on evidence," Vance told reporters. Trump, meanwhile, has taken credit for pressing Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang and said that his administration assured the company's officials that Huang did not present a national security risk. The president has staked the nation's economic growth on artificial intelligence, and worried Huang's ouster was tanking the stock market . Trump also saw Huang's ouster as risking putting the U.S. behind Beijing in the race for dominance in the field if Huang, widely seen by backers and critics as a generational talent in AI, were to be poached by a Chinese firm. The president earlier this week said Vance, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were among administration officials he enlisted to make the case to Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang. White House officials deemed Vance, who worked in Silicon Valley before jumping into politics, as having the stature to serve as an effective emissary in helping Nvidia board members overcome their reservations, according to a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity. ___ Madhani reported from Washington. AP writer Mary Clare Jalonick in Washington contributed to this report. articles.title: Trump’s new tariff plan would bring back much of what the Supreme Court struck down
articles.summary: A new wave of tariffs from the White House would move overall rates almost exactly back to where they stood in early 2026, according to one initial analysis of the new duties. The Yale Budget Lab says the newly unveiled plans , if enacted, would return the US to rates seen just before the Supreme Court struck down President Trump's blanket tariffs in February. Read more: 5 ways to tariff-proof your finances The estimated overall average statutory rate would rise from the current 11.4% to 13.9% early next year. The rate in February, just before the high court struck down Trump's tariffs enacted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977 (IEEPA), was 13.8%. That remains well below the overall rates seen in 2025. The group estimates that 2025 rates exceeded 15%, peaking at nearly 23% in the weeks after "Liberation Day" in April 2025. "The administration said it wanted to rebuild the IEEPA tariff regime using Section 301; with this proposal, it will have done so in the aggregate," the group said in its analysis. The mix of countries bearing the duties will shift slightly, the budget lab noted, with apparel, electronics, and appliances among the biggest categories affected by the new duties. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on the South Lawn of the White House on Tuesday. (Mehmet Eser/Anadolu via Getty Images) Anadolu via Getty Images The reaction from other corners, meanwhile, was that a combination of widespread exemptions, smaller rate changes on other trading partners, and many tariffs that will not be stacked meant the impact could be smaller. "The latest US tariff announcement is not as alarming as it looks," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist at Capital Economics, wrote in an analysis. "The increase in the effective tariff rate looks set to be a touch lower than we've been assuming for our forecasts, although the new tariffs will still provide a marginal boost to prices and keep core goods inflation firm into next year," he added, noting that an exact projection from his group will come later on. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer downplayed the macroeconomic effects in a CNBC appearance Wednesday, describing the total changes as moves that "really will just top up a few percentage points." He added that the higher rates on China — the one place where the new tariffs are set to stack on top of other tariffs — are an exception and that the situation for most countries will be less dramatic. A new 'deal rate' for dozens of countries One major trading partner dodged new tariffs this week when it was announced that an investigation in Mexico was still being reviewed. Greer added that recent talks have been going well. Canada was also not subject to this eight-month investigation, which wrapped up this week and covered China, the European Union, and 14 other nations. The visitors' entrance to the U.S. Trade Representative's office is seen in 2024 in Washington. (J. David Ake/Getty Images) J. David Ake via Getty Images China is set for a 20% baseline "deal rate," which could jump to 40% if ongoing talks break down, while other partners will see much more modest changes. Rates on some EU goods will jump from 10% to 15% if the new tariffs on excess structural capacity go forward and replace previous tariffs imposed around the issue of forced labor. Yet the exemption for an array of goods that the EU and others enjoy includes key products such as semiconductors, as well as automobiles, steel, and aluminum, which are subject to a separate tariff authority. Other goods the Trump administration has carved out in recent months, notably certain energy and food products, will also be exempted. Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance. articles.title: Army official says all 5 tons of lead azide were successfully destroyed in Iowa
articles.summary: The U.S. Army detonated 5 tons of unstable bomb-making chemicals as part of a controlled explosion on Wednesday morning, despite a legal battle over the potential health and environmental impacts from the dust. The explosion detonated the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide, a highly sensitive explosive material, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The Army has released maps showing where the dust could drift and warned people to avoid the area, adding that children under 6 and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to lead exposure. The detonation followed an appeals court decision that found adequate safeguards to protect the community were in place. Officials have been taking steps to mitigate the risk, such as barriers around the blast zone. In leaflets handed out to local residents, the Army said the chemicals had degraded, becoming "extremely unstable and sensitive to even slight friction or movement" — meaning there is a risk of an explosion if they attempt to move or store the chemicals any longer. The Environmental Protection Agency said it had granted an emergency permit to detonate 68 drums of the lead azide because a "controlled detonation during optimal weather conditions and incorporating robust mitigation measures, compared to an uncontrolled explosion, significantly reduces the potential reach and concentration of lead dust landing on surfaces, such as homes and windows." Officials in Missouri and Illinois are also monitoring the situation . articles.title: Oil prices rise after alleged Houthi attack on Saudi refinery
articles.summary: By Nicole Jao and Anna Hirtenstein NEW YORK, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Crude oil prices rallied on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, raising concerns about unexpected Middle ‌East supply disruptions that could cut against expectations for a coming global surplus. Brent crude futures settled $3.21, or 3.5%, ‌higher at $94.61 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed $1.63, or 2%, to $83.68. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis ​said on Wednesday that they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district. The refinery, Saudi Arabia's largest, is part of a complex that also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude. The Houthi statement triggered Wednesday's price rally, said PVM oil analyst Tamas Varga, citing a rising geopolitical risk premium. Traders were also likely covering short positions ahead ‌of the US Thanksgiving holiday, Varga said. Investors ⁠are nervous about the geopolitical tension going into the weekend, said Phil Flynn, an analyst at Price Futures Group. US CRUDE STOCKS RISE LESS THAN ANTICIPATED US crude stocks rose by 1.1 ⁠million barrels to 418.9 million barrels in the week ended November 20, the Energy Information Administration said. Analysts in a Reuters poll expected a 1.5 million-barrel rise. [EIA/S] The inventory report pushed prices higher as the market was expecting a bigger inventory build, Flynn said. The ​uncertainty surrounding ​OPEC+ ahead of its November 29 meeting, where they will ​decide on their 2027 output policy, has held ‌prices in check. The United Arab Emirates is no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies, and Iraq is looking to boost its oil capacity, said Zhenqiang Seto, an oil research specialist at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will ‌be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno added. Russian Deputy Prime Minister ​Alexander Novak said OPEC+ is set to complete a review of member ​production capacities by year-end. Iraq and Kazakhstan were pressing ​OPEC+ to raise its estimate of their oil production capacity, said four people familiar with ‌the matter, heightening tensions over a review that will ​help determine how much members ​can pump next year. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline reopened, ending a brief halt after what the National Oil Corporation described as an unlawful group closed a valve. In the Strait of Hormuz, a container ship was targeted and came to a ​stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route ‌near the strait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards told state media. articles.title: 2nd federal judge blocks Trump's latest bid to restrict birthright citizenship
articles.summary: A second federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Trump administration’s latest attempts to restrict birthright citizenship. U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper of Washington, D.C. ordered a preliminary injunction in a 67-page memorandum opinion , in which he asserted the Citizenship Clause of the 14th Amendment "promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States.” The judge also said the court will prevent federal authorities from enforcing the president’s August executive orders, which sought to limit the scope of birthright citizenship and combat “birth tourism” — which involves traveling to another country for the primary purpose of giving birth on its soil so the child automatically has citizenship. articles.title: NASA deliberately crashed into an asteroid. Now scientists are surveying the damage.
articles.summary: The asteroid before (left) and after, showing the crater left behind by a spacecraft's impact [ESA] The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface. The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision. "The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team. "It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful." The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h). It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 6,200 miles long (10,000km), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space. Dimorphos is about 150m (500ft) wide and was partly chosen as the target because it is one of an asteroid pair -  it orbits around a larger space rock called Didymos, which is about 730m (2,400ft) wide. The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid. Before the collision, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes. Watch: Moment Nasa spacecraft leaves stadium-sized crater in asteroid A key objective of the Hera mission is to measure the mass of Dimorphos, in order to work out how effective the spacecraft's shove was. This information would be vital if we ever spotted a space rock that was on a collision course with Earth. "It would help us to predict what would happen if we had to hit another asteroid," said Prof Simon Green, a planetary scientist who is on Hera's science team. "We [could] measure its properties and say: 'Well, we need this mass of spacecraft, travelling at this speed, this early, in order to deflect it enough so that it misses the Earth'." Hera's arrival on the scene is helping scientists answer many more questions too. Not only did the collision alter the shape of Dimorphos, it also changed the way it moves. "Before the Dart impact, Dimorphos was more like our own Moon - so it was always showing the same face to Didymos, and it was behaving quite nicely," explained Raducan. "Now it's very, very chaotic - it's tumbling. Imagine a barrel that you throw down the stairs, and the barrel is rolling and it's moving, and basically that's what Dimorphos does right now around Didymos." Hera has also taken detailed images of Didymos, revealing its surface in detail. "The gravity at the surface of Didymos is about 40,000 times less than the gravity on Earth," said Naomi Murdoch, who is on the Hera mission team. "We can already see some fascinating and complex geology. We can see regions of boulders. "The smallest details that we can make out in these images are about 3m in size. So that means that all the boulders that you can see with your eyes are at least 3m big, and some as big as 10m. So what we're seeing here is boulders the size of cars and buses sitting on a world with almost no gravity." The mission has sent back new pictures of the smaller Dimorphos orbiting around Didymos [ESA] The Hera mission will spend the next six months studying Dimorphos and Didymos, sending back more images taken from closer up in higher resolution. "Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact," said Patrick Michel, principal investigator of ESA's Hera mission. The spacecraft is packed with instruments and also has two shoe-boxed sized satellites onboard, which can study the impact site up close, and then later land on the asteroid. But the first images taken by Hera have also revealed a new challenge. Dimorphos and Didymos are travelling through space surrounded by hundreds of boulders ranging in size from tens of centimetres to metre-size rocks. This will make it especially challenging to operate the spacecraft and cube satellites through this boulder field. A long trail of debris from the collision was spotted by the Hubble Space Telescope  [NASA/Hubble Space Telescope] This was the last image from Dart before it crashed into Dimorphos in 2022 [NASA/Johns Hopkins APL] Asteroids pose a significant threat to our planet. The biggest, which measures more than a kilometre across, could cause global devastation. But medium-sized asteroids around the same dimensions as Dimorphos could wipe out a city. "We all know what happened to the dinosaurs, right? And we don't want that to happen to us," said Carolyn Ernst at Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, who has worked on both the Dart and Hera missions. "The good news for us is that there are far fewer potential threats out there in the Solar System than there were millions of years ago. But there are objects out there." She said the biggest asteroids have been spotted, and none are heading to Earth. "The smallest stuff isn't too much of a threat because our atmosphere protects us," she added. "But there's a size range in the middle where we don't know where all of them are, and it could, if impacted, cause problems for humanity. And if we can find out about that and know about that, well, we sure as heck would want to try to stop that." Artist's impression showing Hera. It has two small satellites on board to study the asteroid up close [ESA] Scientists want to gather as much intelligence as they can about space rocks to make us as well equipped as possible to deal with whatever the Universe throws at us. A new mission is launching in 2027 to track potentially hazardous asteroids - a space telescope called the Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor. There are also more visits planned to asteroids, including to one called Apophis, which is about 450m (1,480ft) long. Apophis was discovered in 2004 and it was initially thought it might hit the Earth as early as 13 April 2029. But now scientists understand its orbit better, and say it won't hit us for at least the next 100 years. Instead of a crash in 2029, it will fly just 32,000km (20,000 miles) above our surface. This will give scientists the rare chance to study a space rock up-close. Two spacecraft will head to Apophis, including Nasa's Osiris-Apex (which previously grabbed a sample from another asteroid called Bennu) and Ramses, a joint mission between ESA and the Japanese Space Agency (JAXA). articles.title: How the FAA's new Line Up and Wait rules may impact Thanksgiving holiday air travel
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration imposed new standards for its Line Up and Wait airport policy on Tuesday that, though not a significant change, could affect travelers during the busy holiday travel season. Line Up and Wait (LUAW) is a procedure that allows planes preparing for departure from busy airports to taxi into position on the runway while they wait to be cleared for takeoff. It’s designed to make airport departures more efficient by putting planes in position to take off as soon as airspace has been cleared. Under the FAA’s new policy , airports can still use LUAW, but they must designate a watch supervisor whose sole job is to oversee LUAW operations and whose attention cannot be split by other tasks. The new rules change guidance from saying that airports “should” have a dedicated LUAW supervisor to saying that they “must” have one. The FAA said the change is intended to “elevate the safety standard” for LUAW operations by “removing ambiguity” about staffing requirements under the old rules. Will the new rules affect Thanksgiving holiday travel? The impact of the policy change on passengers comes down to staffing. At airports with enough staff to assign one person exclusively to LUAW, the effect will likely be minimal. But airports that may be short-staffed, a chronic problem in recent years, might be unable to use LUAW. That could mean slightly longer waits on the tarmac in some cases. Even minor delays caused by the new LUAW policy could be compounded by potential disruptions from the Thanksgiving travel rush , with 417,000 flights expected to depart during the 9-day holiday travel period and stormy weather forecast for both coasts. The new LUAW rules will also be in place for the December holiday travel season. They are scheduled to expire in June. FAA under scrutiny Though the new policy represents a relatively minor procedural update, it comes at a time when the FAA is under intense scrutiny following the historically disruptive nationwide ground stop that resulted in the cancellation of 18,000 flights earlier this month. That outage, plus a series of smaller technical disruptions in the weeks since, has fueled a sense of “outage anxiety” among holiday travelers. In a recent YouGov poll, 72% of respondents said they were concerned about "flight cancellations or significant delays as a result of further disruptions to U.S. air travel" over the holiday travel season. Nearly a third said the ground stop could potentially lead them to alter their travel plans. The new LUAW rules are not related to the ground stop or other recent disruptions. They were first proposed in early October, more than a month before the ground stop occurred. There were no reports of significant delays related to the new rules on Tuesday, the first day they were in effect and the busiest day of the Thanksgiving travel season. Congress is debating whether to provide the FAA with billions of dollars in additional funding to upgrade its infrastructure and implement other changes to prevent future outages. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has asked for $50 billion , but even lawmakers who support a funding boost for the FAA say the final price tag could be much smaller. The debate could affect LUAW operations at the nation’s airports, depending on whether Congress approves funding to help them address staffing shortages that may limit their ability to assign someone exclusively to LUAW. articles.title: Inflation remains high despite retreating gas prices, highlighting challenges for the Fed
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge showed prices heated up more than expected in October, all but guaranteeing the central bank will raise interest rates next month, with the prospect of further hikes in the first quarter. The "core" Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, picked up steam last month, rising 3.3%, compared with expectations for 3.2% and up from 3.1% in September. Month over month, core prices held steady at 0.3%, in line with projections. On a headline basis, PCE was in line with expectations for 3.8%, up from 3.6% in September. Month over month, PCE moderated, rising 0.3% as expected and down from 0.5% previously. "The continued strength in core PCE inflation … make[s] a December rate hike certain," said Bradley Saunders, economist for Capital Economics. "While we still think a 25bp hike is the most likely course of action at next month's meeting, the strength of the data means a follow-up hike in January could also be necessary." Sauders noted that the latest data boosted the three-month annualized rate of inflation to 3.6%, from an upwardly revised 3%. Core goods price pressures almost doubled to 0.35% month over month, as energy prices continued to feed through, taking the annual rate to 2.3%, from 2%. Services price growth was also strong, up 0.28% month over month, led by recreational services and food and accommodation services. But Mike Skordeles, head of US economics for Truist Advisory Services, isn't too alarmed by Wednesday's report, noting that the comparisons from last year's data were much lower, making the numbers look hotter. Skordeles expects the same trend to continue in November, as both headline and core were equally below trend in 2025. "The overall inflation trajectory is largely unchanged, especially when excluding food and energy," said Skordeles. Most Fed officials have already coalesced around a rate hike next month, though some have called for more aggressive action than others. Wednesday's report may seal that action for some members. Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation Fed governor Chris Waller said that if the central bank hikes by a quarter point next month, it will need to signal a follow-up hike of the same size in January — or else deliver a jumbo half-percentage-point increase in December. Fed governor Lisa Cook echoed that urgency on Friday, arguing that financial conditions remain too accommodative while inflation remains stubbornly high. She warned the central bank risks falling behind the curve if it doesn't hike now. New York Fed president John Williams, however, has pushed back against calls for supersize rate hikes , saying last week that he doesn't think the situation calls for "dramatic action." Williams said earlier this week that the Fed needs to take a more forward-looking approach to inflation and thus to setting rates, noting that monetary policy works with a lag of one to two years to have its maximum effect on the economy. His statement that the Fed needs to be more forward-looking does not align with its approach in recent years. The central bank has tended to be data-dependent, which is inherently more backward-looking. Williams didn't suggest that the Fed not consult data, but rather that any actions taken today will take a year or two to be implemented. But new tariffs being proposed of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other nations could boost inflation. One reason Williams has been sanguine about the inflation outlook is he believes tariffs have largely washed out of the picture. However, he's also said that would change if new tariffs were put in place. The administration's latest proposal could mean new tariffs take effect early next year, pending comments, hearings and further negotiations. That raises the prospect of further rate hikes and holding rates higher for longer. Follow Jennifer Schonberger on X @Jenniferisms and on Instagram . articles.title: Trump says Iran war 'funded' through January until Democrats take control of Congress
articles.summary: Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway. Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities. See the most recent developments below. Latest Developments Nov 25, 9:28 AM Renewed Yemen fighting displaces 364,000, UN official says Renewed fighting in Yemen's civil war has forced more than 364,000 people from their homes since August, including tens of thousands over the past week, the United Nations' humanitarian chief said in a statement Wednesday after he arrived in the port city of Aden in the south of the country. "Fighting, insecurity and heavy restrictions along key supply routes are preventing families from accessing the food and medicine they need to survive," UN Under Secretary General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher said, noting that half of Yemen's population needs aid. "Millions are hungry," he added. Fletcher also called on the Houthi rebels to "immediately and unconditionally release our detained UN colleagues and other humanitarians." "Our work and our people must be protected," he said. Since 2014, Yemen's internationally-recognized, Saudi-backed government -- now based in Aden -- has been fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis, which occupy the capital Sana'a. The conflict has become a widening front in the regional war involving Iran that began in February. In a video statement, Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the operation against the financial district in Riyadh "caused extensive damage." The Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province was also targeted, causing "fires to break out there," Saree said. Early on Wednesday morning, a Saudi military spokesman said four drones had been intercepted in Ras Tanura and "a number of fragments fell as a result of the interception, with no casualties." Satellite images showed black smoke above the Ras Tanura oil refinery on Wednesday. Nasa Worldview/via Reuters - PHOTO: A satellite image shows a large smoke cloud billowing over Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery on Nov. 25, 2026. -ABC News' Nasser Atta and Othon Leyva Nov 25, 2:55 AM Trump says Iran war 'funded' through January President Donald Trump said the ongoing war with Iran is "funded" through January, when Democrats take control of Congress and could reign in his authority to authorize the conflict. In an interview with the New York Post conducted in the Oval Office on Tuesday afternoon, Trump said the incoming Democratic majority will "take a total win and make it a loss." Trump again touted the U.S. military success against Iran. "Their navy's gone, their air force is gone, their anti-aircraft, everything's gone. Their leaders are gone. I mean, if [Democrats] do that, they'll just take a win and make it a loss," Trump said. When pressed on whether his timeframe to freely launch renewed strikes is narrowing, Trump reportedly said he finds it "hard to believe" that Democrats would stop the war. "I don't know how they could do that politically, because we have a win. We can put that war to bed anytime we want," Trump said, according to the Post. Israel's goal of ending the Islamic Republic is "probably doable," Trump also said, but told the Post that regime change is not his goal. "I just don't want them to have a nuclear weapon. I was never for or against regime change, that was never a criteria for me," Trump said. Trump also addressed an Iranian announcement this week that it would be suing the U.S. for compensation for an airstrike on a school. "Well, I want compensation for the people that they've killed, which is far more because they've killed, first of all, they killed 75,000 protesters in the last seven months. But they've killed our people for years," Trump replied, according to the Post. "The USS Cole, they've killed many, many hundreds of Americans. So if they want to play the compensation game, we win," the president said. -ABC News' Isabella Murray Nov 24, 11:49 AM US investigating whether Iran is behind tanker cyberattacks The U.S. is investigating whether Iran is behind a series of cyberattacks that targeted energy tankers, according to multiple officials. At least 50 ships are believed to have been attacked, with some receiving bomb threats that purported to say the ship was to be detonated. The U.S. has identified Iran as the prime suspect, but are also investigating whether Russia could also be the suspect. The threats are believed to scare boats into not traversing overseas. The Coast Guard has helped thwart all of the cyber attacks, according to officials. They've also posted a warning on their website telling tankers to patch their systems, prior to a cyber event occurring. "Just as we monitor for mechanical or weather-related hazards, we incorporate cyber risk management into our routine, professional approach to facilitating commerce and ensuring safe vessel transits into and from our ports and waterway," according to a Coast Guard spokesperson. Earlier this year, two boats headed to Texas were boarded by U.S. Coast Guard teams after it was discovered that cyber incidents occurred onboard. Nov 24, 9:11 AM Riyadh tower targeted in attack, Saudi spokesperson says A tower in the financial district of the Saudi capital Riyadh was targeted in a "terrorist attack," a Saudi military spokesman said Tuesday. "One of the towers of the financial center was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack," Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki, the spokesman for Saudi-led coalition forces fighting the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, posted on X. The post did not provide details about the nature of the attack. One of the towers in the Riyadh financial center was damaged last week when it was hit by a projectile. -ABC News' Othon Leyva Nov 24, 9:03 AM UKMTO reports attacks on 3 tankers in Strait of Hormuz on Monday The United Kingdom Maritime Operations (UKMTO) Centre on Tuesday issued a warning after it received a report of three vessels being struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday evening. The vessels were reported to have continued their transit with all crew members accounted for, UKMTO said. Separately, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy on Tuesday claimed that several tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Republic News Agency reported. The IRGC Navy said the vessels were traveling through the strait "illegally." The IRGC has repeatedly claimed vessels have been damaged by naval mines, but U.S. Central Command has called previous claims false. -ABC News' Othon Leyva Nov 24, 6:27 AM Iranian army chief threatens 'unimaginable' response to any new infrastructure attacks Army chief Maj. "We have now developed new operational plans to implement these new strategies and have made the necessary preparations," Hatami said, as quoted by the semi-official Mehr News Agency. "Should our infrastructure be struck again, we will strike their infrastructure in a way that is not easily reversible," he added. Nov 24, 4:09 AM Ship attacked off UAE on Sunday, UKMTO says The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre on Tuesday confirmed that a bulk carrier was hit by an "unknown projectile" while at anchor off the coast of the United Arab Emirates on Sunday. The incident occurred 23 nautical miles northeast of the Emirati east coast city of Khor Fakkan, the UKMTO alert said. "A fire was reported onboard the vessel but no casualties have been reported at this time," the alert said. Nov 24, 3:43 AM US land blockade of Iran 'impossible,' Araghchi says Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Monday that the proposed U.S. land blockade of his country "is impossible, both because of the country's vastness and the large number of provinces." U.S. Central Command announced earlier this month the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, which would be assigned "to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials." In comments published by the IRIB state broadcaster on Tuesday, Araghchi said Iran's "extensive connections with neighboring provinces in neighboring countries, high traffic and people-to-people ties, and historical and cultural roots on both sides of the border," meant that the U.S. task force would fail. "There are capacities in the country's provinces, especially the border provinces, that can open what the enemy wants to close to us," he added. "The duty of the country and the people is to discourage the enemies from imposing sanctions; the best way to counter these pressures is to discourage the sanctions takers from achieving their goals so that they know that this tool is not and will not be effective," Araghchi said. "Of course, this does not mean abandoning the other duty of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which is to open diplomatic channels for negotiations and lifting sanctions, and that path is also ongoing," he continued. -ABC News' Desiree Adib Nov 23, 6:49 AM Trump says Iran launched more attacks in past week than at any time 'for over a year' President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Sunday night that "Iran has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year." "Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage," Trump said of the Iranian attacks. Reported attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz have been higher in number in October and November than any previous months since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in late February, according to data compiled by maritime organizations and analyzed by ABC News. articles.title: 美国拟对配额外食糖大幅加征关税，直指巴西
articles.summary: 特朗普政府提议对不受配额制度覆盖的食糖大幅加征关税，主要针对全球最大产糖国巴西，此举可能进一步推高本已高于国际市场的美国国内糖价。 美国贸易代表办公室周三提出，对配额外原糖征收每公斤44美分关税，对配额外精制糖征收每公斤60美分关税。 这一提案的影响范围超出预期：除巴西外，还可能适用于所有国家，以防其他国家填补巴西留下的市场空缺。 美国贸易大使Jamieson Greer在提案随附的新闻稿中表示，全面征税是为了“防止来自其他国家的食糖进口激增，巴西的市场缺口可能由这些国家填补”。 消息公布后，纽约原糖期货周三一度上涨4.6%，伦敦精制糖期货一度上涨3.8%。 受冲击最大的可能是美国国内糖价：现行贸易限制已使美国糖价相对国际市场存在溢价，而仅拟对原糖征收的关税，就已高于全球期货价格水平。 美国国内糖价首当其冲 “影响更多会体现在美国国内市场，”长期跟踪食糖的分析师Mike McDougall表示，美国国内糖价“将上涨，直到足以覆盖关税成本，尤其是如果美国产量进一步下调的话”。 美国每年通过配额制度允许一定数量的食糖以较低成本进入本国，另有一项贸易协议允许墨西哥每年按不同数量对美出口食糖。 二十多年来，超出这些额度的食糖一直需缴纳每公斤33到36美分的关税。新提案的税率较现行水平明显提高。 种植商与食品制造商立场对立 美国甘蔗和甜菜种植者一直推动提高关税，以阻止他们眼中享受不公平补贴的外国供应进入，近年来超出配额进入美国市场的食糖数量有所增加。 巴西通常是配额外食糖的最大供应国，但每当美国对巴西的关税上升，阿根廷等国也会增加对美出口。 食品制造商长期以来反对推高美国糖价的政策，并认为，作为最后手段进口的供应不应被额外收费。 据美国农业部数据，由于种植面积减少和虫害蔓延，2026-27年度美国食糖产量预计将降至七年低点，这将抬高美国的进口需求。 对巴西的针对性施压 据一位了解情况的巴西官员称，这项新提案令人意外，其中还包括对巴西飞机加征更高关税。该官员表示，两国关于降低贸易壁垒的谈判已停滞数月。 对食糖加征更高关税，与特朗普政府近期逐步扩大农产品关税豁免的趋势相悖，此前获豁免的包括可可、咖啡和橙汁等美国国内产量不足的品类。 美国食品杂货价格正在上涨，反映出能源成本上升正向食品供应链传导，以及异常强烈的厄尔尼诺现象的影响。 但特朗普也一直对巴西采取更强硬的关税措施。此前对巴西加征的关税中，曾提及巴西对美国乙醇征收关税，使美国生物燃料失去一个重要市场。Greer周三表示，最新举措为美国提供了“更大的筹码”，以推动巴西改变政策。 “我们真诚希望这一行动能促使巴西回到谈判桌前，就改善两国乙醇贸易进行善意讨论，”美国乙醇行业组织可再生燃料协会主席Geoff Cooper在声明中表示。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

年首届航展以来，珠海航展已发展成为全球重要的综合性航空航天及防务展览平台。本届航展有望集中呈现我国军工全产业链最新成果。无人作战方面，大型隐身无人机、异构蜂群及低成本巡飞弹持续发展，反无人装备向激光、微波、电子干扰与传统防空武器协同升级；航空装备方面，新一代战机、航空发动机及先进材料技术进展值得关注；防务及航天领域，多层防空反导、无人地面装备、先进雷达及可重复使用火箭等有望成为重要看点。全球沿海国家海防、防空采购需求持续上行，国产海洋防务+防空装备性价比优势凸显，珠海航展是国内军贸最重要的展示、洽谈平台，展会前后容易持续释放订单、型号官宣等催化，海防+防空预警军贸赛道迎来阶段性行情窗口。 5、 6G | 据证券时报报道，工信部批复多省市开展 6G 创新发展部省协同试点，标志国内 6G 商业化筹备进入落地推进阶段。试点围绕关键技术攻关、空天地一体化场景测试、产业配套完善、标准体系搭建推进，加速补齐产业链短板，推动核心器件、通信设备、卫星融合、智能感知等环节迭代升级。相较于前代通信体系，6G 实现空天地海全域覆盖，融合通感一体、算力网络、泛在智能能力，可落地低空经济、卫星通信、工业互联网、无人装备等多元场景，长期成长空间广阔。随着试点铺开，高端天线、射频器件、通信芯片、仿真测试设备、卫星配套等环节持续受益，产业链有望开启长周期迭代，头部企业持续收获技术落地与订单增量红利。 6、 高带宽存储器HBM | 据中证报报道， 华为 将在ISSCC 2027上展示自研HBM和逻辑堆叠技术。根据IEEE官方11月23日公布的ISSCC 2027议程草案，这些成果覆盖移动SoC、AI处理器供电、高速互连和高带宽内存四大方向。最受关注的是自研HBM内存方案，采用‌64通道、4096个DQ数据接口‌，位宽是HBM4标准2048bit的‌两倍‌，并使用‌5层晶圆对晶圆（W2W）混合键合‌技术，同时把内存控制器集成进堆叠结构。 7、 冰雪产业 | 据中证报报道，随着气温走低，国内“滑雪”搜索量暴涨，冷资源持续释放热效应。冰雪消费热度走高，产业供给同步提速。冰雪运动持续升温，滑雪装备需求快速增长，高性价比国产雪具、智能穿戴设备受到雪友青睐。不少企业靠技术创新开拓市场，国产冰雪装备加速突围。据报道，在张家口宣化产业园内，全自动造雪机、国产化索道订单爆满。新款造雪机订单已经排到2029年，出口俄罗斯等地。滑雪索道也摆脱进口依赖，实现自主研发量产。 8、 半导体 | 据中证报报道，二维半导体专用产线设备商基元科技完成数千万元天使轮融资，由朝晖芯华基金领投，宁创投、常州高新投、南慧创投等跟投，云岫资本担任后续融资财务顾问。募集资金将重点用于高端定制化设备研发及产业化推进。据公开资料显示，基元科技产品覆盖二维半导体集成电路制造“生长—转移—检测”全流程。公司自研的高温原位光学观测CVD设备（CVV）为全球唯一商业化的同类机型；另自主设计全球首台二维半导体晶圆转移产线装备，并承接国内二维半导体中试线的晶圆级转移、检测订单。二维半导体（又称原子层半导体）被视为后摩尔时代延续芯片性能增长的关键技术路径。随着硅基晶体管微缩逼近物理极限，二维半导体凭借其原子级厚度、强栅控能力和低功耗优势，正从实验室加速走向产业化。 articles.title: OpenAI与马斯克年内第二次庭审交锋：聘请Cravath顶级律师迎战
articles.summary: OpenAI已指定Cravath, Swaine & Moore律所顶级合伙人Gary Bornstein担任首席辩护律师，应对马斯克旗下公司在得克萨斯州联邦法院提起的诉讼。该案将于明年3月在Fort Worth由陪审团审理，距马斯克在加州另一起诉讼中败诉尚不足一年。 据路透报道， Bornstein是Cravath诉讼部门联席负责人，将担任该案的首席庭审律师。马斯克一方则由Bartlit Beck律所的John Hughes担任首席庭审律师，该所曾代理哈佛大学招生平权案并最终打到美国最高法院。 这起案件由X Corp与SpaceX Super Intelligence于去年提起，指控苹果与OpenAI合谋垄断生成式AI聊天机器人市场。苹果已于9月与马斯克旗下公司达成和解，双方均未披露条款。 对投资者而言，这场庭审是马斯克与OpenAI持续多年的法律对抗的延续，也关系到生成式AI市场的竞争格局界定。案件由美国地区法官Mark Pittman审理。 Cravath与Bartlit Beck领衔法庭交锋 OpenAI除Cravath外，还聘请了Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz，团队成员包括Stephen DiPrima和Kevin Schwartz。 Bornstein与Cravath的Lauren Moskowitz同时还在代理“Fortnite”开发商Epic Games对苹果应用商店业务的诉讼，Bornstein在该案中担任首席律师。 马斯克旗下公司除Bartlit Beck外，还由Axinn Veltrop和Stone Hilton的律师代理。 Hughes所在的Bartlit Beck曾在2018年代理一宗起诉哈佛大学招生做法的案件，该案促成了美国最高法院终止高校招生中考虑种族的裁决。 年内第二场审判延续双方法律冲突 这是马斯克与OpenAI在不到一年内的第二次庭审交锋。今年5月，加州奥克兰联邦法院的陪审团裁定马斯克败诉，该案指控OpenAI背离了其创立时造福人类的初衷。 OpenAI由Sam Altman、马斯克等人在2015年创立，马斯克于2018年退出董事会，OpenAI次年开始设立营利性业务。 案件名称为X Corp and SpaceXAI v OpenAI，受理法院为美国得克萨斯州北区联邦地区法院，案号4:25-cv-00914-P。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 关税压顶：市场有多害怕
articles.summary: 11月25日，特朗普政府宣布对14个经济体加征新关税，税率从15%到35%不等，最快明年1月底落地。欧盟、日本、韩国、越南、印度——无论盟友还是新兴替代供应商，全部在名单上。 消息一出，感恩节前最后一个完整交易日，纳斯达克盘中暴跌4%，道指一度蒸发近千点。恐慌指数 VIX 单月飙升超过60%，创下新冠疫情以来最猛的月度涨幅。纳斯达克100指数从历史高点回落20%，踩到了熊市线。 奇怪的是，那天公布的经济数据并不差：三季度 GDP 增长4.3%，制造业连续10个月扩张。美国经济发动机明明在轰鸣，市场却听见了另一种断裂的声音。

articles.title: AI债务风险加剧！CoreWeave、英伟达信用违约风险指标双双创历史新高
articles.summary: CoreWeave和英伟达五年期信用违约互换成本双双刷新纪录，CoreWeave违约概率被市场定价至逾70%。 据彭博报道， CoreWeave和英伟达的信用风险指标周三刷新历史最高水平，衡量市场担忧程度的广泛指标也再度回到3月份时的水平。 华尔街对科技行业为人工智能融资而进行的创纪录借贷日益担忧。同日纳指100一度跌破20%的牛熊分界线。 ICE Data Services数据显示， CoreWeave五年期债务违约保护成本一度上升2.09个百分点，为史上最大单日涨幅，达到每年15.34个百分点。掉期市场对该公司未来五年内违约的概率定价已超过70%。 英伟达、谷歌、甲骨文和SpaceX的信用违约互换也在周三创下最新纪录高位。 担忧正从债券市场蔓延至股市，纳斯达克100指数周三一度较上月峰值下跌20%，触及进入熊市的门槛。 AI相关债券领跌，分化扩散至全板块 AI相关债券是当日二级市场交易中跌幅最大的品种之一，但周三的疲软并不限于AI领域，各板块普遍走弱。 市场上衡量美国企业债风险感知的S&P Dow Jones Indices CDX投资级指数利差一度走阔3.1个基点，至65.63个基点，为3月31日以来盘中最高。高收益信用债的同类指标也创下3月31日以来的最差水平。 Allspring Global Investments高级固定收益交易员Mark Clegg对彭博表示， 投资者现在面临的核心问题是当前利差究竟是“便宜货还是下落的刀”。 “黑色星期五的折扣出现在了AI债券上，”他说，“价值显然比此前更多了，但价格发现的过程还没有结束。” DoubleLine Capital的Robert Cohen此前曾警告该板块存在潜在泡沫，但他认为当前的价格与收益率已经反映了潜在风险，值得买入。 AI回报忧虑同步冲击股市与债市 此轮信用风险的焦点在于科技企业以创纪录规模的债务融资支撑AI资本开支， 市场对这类支出的回报心存疑虑，担忧同时冲击了债务与股票两个市场。 CoreWeave作为AI算力租赁的代表性企业，其信用保护成本单日涨幅创历史之最，成为本轮担忧最集中的观察窗口。 英伟达、Alphabet、甲骨文等大型科技公司的CDS同步创下纪录，显示风险定价已从单一标的扩散至整个AI产业链的融资端。 对投资者而言，关键变量是价格发现何时结束——利差走阔意味着风险补偿提升，但也意味着在信用事件真正落地前，估值仍可能继续承压。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 11月26日会员早报：美国核心PCE超预期升至3.3% 胡塞武装袭击沙特最大炼油厂
articles.summary: 1、【美国核心PCE超预期升至3.3%】美国商务部经济分析局（BEA）当地时间11月25日（周三）公布，10月PCE价格指数同比上涨3.8%，与预期一致；剔除食品和能源的核心PCE同比上涨3.3%，高于3.2%的预期。按9月年度修订后的现行数据，整体读数3.845%是2023年5月以来最高，9月修正值为3.67%，相当于三年半新高；核心读数3.26%是2023年11月以来最高，前值上修至3.14%。这是12月议息会议前最后一份PCE数据，CME FedWatch显示市场对12月加息的定价约为98%。 2、【胡塞武装袭击沙特最大炼油厂】 也门胡塞武装周三（11月25日）对沙特最大炼油厂拉斯坦努拉（Ras Tanura）发动无人机袭击，并威胁把沙特红海港口列为打击目标，市场因此重新计入中东冲突扰乱能源供应的风险溢价。布伦特原油期货周三早些时候一度跌至每桶89.50美元，随后扭转跌势，升至92美元上方。 3、【美国三季度GDP增速创三年来最快】美国商务部经济分析局（BEA）11月25日公布了三季度GDP的二次估算。美国第三季度实际GDP按年率计算增长4.3%，比10月底公布的初值3.4%上修0.9个百分点，接近二季度2.2%的两倍。这是美国经济三年来最快的季度增速。 4、【美国10月耐用品订单仅增0.2%，远低于预期】美国商务部周三（11月25日）公布的初值数据显示，10月美国耐用品订单环比增长0.2%，增加8亿美元至3467亿美元，远低于市场预期的0.7%，较9月修正后的2.0%明显放缓。不过，这已是耐用品订单过去8个月里第7个月增长。放缓主要来自运输设备。剔除运输设备后，10月订单环比增长0.5%，与9月增速持平。 5、【韩股再入清算模式】韩国股市再度进入清算模式。11月25日，KOSPI指数暴跌6.16%（308.52点），收于4697.51点，前一交易日的涨幅全部回吐。这是1月13日以来的最低收盘，也是本轮AI行情调整启动以来的最低水平。三星电子重挫9.87%至170,700韩元，市值自3月31日以来首次跌破1000万亿韩元；SK海力士暴跌11.05%至103万韩元。外资当日净卖出约1.95万亿韩元。

articles.title: 标普将英伟达列入“信用观察负面”名单，治理风险成评级焦点
articles.summary: 11月25日周三， 标普全球评级将英伟达的信用评级列入“信用观察负面”名单 ，意味着这家当前评级为“AA”的芯片巨头可能在90天内遭遇下调。 理由在于公司管理层与治理风险上升，这给投资者敲响了信用层面的警钟。 这是英伟达治理风波从董事会层面传导至信用市场的直接体现。本周，董事会先宣布将寻找黄仁勋的继任者，随后又恢复了他的CEO职务，而独立董事委员会对其本人的调查仍在进行中。 据路透社报道， 标普明确表态，这一事件暴露了英伟达管理层与治理框架的脆弱性，尤其是董事会结构、构成与有效性方面的不足。 上周三穆迪已经下调英伟达评级展望。 华尔街见闻提及 ，11月18日，穆迪将英伟达评级展望由“正面”下调至“稳定”，维持Aa1高级无担保债务评级不变。 英伟达股价周三下跌4.7%，自10月6日以来累计已下跌38%；纳斯达克100指数一度逼近较近期高点下跌20%的关口。 下调的时间窗口与幅度：90天，预计一级 标普给出了明确的时间框架与幅度指引。 该机构表示，可能在未来90天内下调英伟达评级，但预计任何潜在下调都将以一级为限，前提是调查及其他信息披露不会损害公司声誉或未来业务前景。 英伟达目前评级为“AA”，表明其具备非常强的偿债能力，最高评级为“AAA”。 尽管评级机构相继调整立场，英伟达的信用基本面并未出现实质恶化。 此前穆迪维持其Aa1评级，这是仅次于最高级别的投资评级，并明确肯定公司财务状况依然“极为强劲”。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 万斯：黄仁勋未受调查，没有任何犯罪证据，根本不需要赦免
articles.summary: 美国副总统万斯周三表示， 黄仁勋“根本不需要赦免”，因为司法部及国家安全部门均确认其未受到调查。 然而，围绕此事的争议远未平息，黄仁勋下周将面临多个国会委员会的质询，英伟达内部调查仍在进行中。 万斯在俄亥俄州赖特-帕特森空军基地向记者表示： “我不认为他需要赦免。我没有看到任何他犯罪的证据。” 他补充称，司法部和多名官员以及国家安全机构告知他， 黄仁勋“没有受到任何调查”，“如果他受到调查，我们显然会告知公众。他没有。” 此番表态是对特朗普总统此前表示愿意给予黄仁勋赦免的回应。特朗普曾公开称黄仁勋已被“洗清”任何潜在的联邦违法嫌疑，并透露自己曾与英伟达董事会成员沟通，力主让这位CEO回归。 周三英伟达一度大跌9%，随后有所反弹，截至发稿下跌4.8%。 董事会决定让黄仁勋回来 万斯被认为在推动黄仁勋回归英伟达一事上发挥了关键的幕后作用。万斯周三解释称： “归根结底，是董事会决定让黄仁勋回来。他显然是一位非常重要的高管。” 特朗普此前也证实，他曾与英伟达董事会成员交谈，主张让黄仁勋回归。总统还声称黄仁勋已被“洗清”嫌疑。 万斯同时强调了政府的国家安全立场：“我们期待英伟达在这方面成为合作伙伴，并遵守美国的出口管制。” 黄仁勋“没有受到任何调查” 美国司法部长Todd Blanche周二多次拒绝确认或否认黄仁勋是否受到调查，但他上周承认，司法部一直在“关注”此事——不过他强调，这与正式调查是两回事。 万斯周三的表态则更为明确，称黄仁勋“没有受到任何调查”。 尽管黄仁勋已于本周一复职，他仍面临英伟达自行下令的内部调查。此外，黄仁勋下周将接受多个国会委员会的质询。 对投资者而言，接下来的关键问题在于：国会听证是否会披露新的信息，以及英伟达内部调查的结论是否会影响管理层稳定性。在AI板块对领导层变动高度敏感的当下，任何新的负面进展都可能再度引发市场波动。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
